claims.text: The catalyst is a platinum-group-metal nanoscale catalyst.
Ethanol oxidation involves transfer of 12 electrons.
Ethanol oxidation involves transfer of 12 protons.
The catalyst's activity is governed by interplay between its oxidation state and local structure.
The catalyst's selectivity is governed by interplay between its oxidation state and local structure.
The catalyst's durability is governed by interplay between its oxidation state and local structure.
The catalyst's oxidation state and local structure change dynamically during ethanol oxidation.
Dynamic coupling between oxidation state and local structure influences the catalytic reaction pathway.
Operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy can elucidate the catalyst's oxidation state and local structure during ethanol oxidation.
Oxidation state and local structure will correlate with catalytic activity.
Oxidation state and local structure will correlate with catalytic selectivity.
Oxidation state and local structure will correlate with catalytic durability.
Absence of correlation between oxidation state or local structure and catalytic performance would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The proposed intervention is an observational measurement rather than a controlled material or reaction change. The baseline without operando monitoring cannot provide corresponding oxidation-state and local-structure measurements, so it does not support the proposed correlation comparison.

The boundary attributes possible failure to limitations of the measurement technique, while the falsification rule treats absence of correlation as decisive evidence against the mechanism; these possibilities are not distinguished.
